parties: Government of India (President, acting through Ministry of Finance) as seller; retail & institutional investors as buyers
headline: India's largest-ever OFS: Government raises ₹31,552 crore (US$3.3 billion) by divesting 6.5% stake in LIC, achieving 10% public shareholding milestone ahead of May 2027 regulatory deadline.
sum: Government of India sold a 6.5% stake in Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) through a two-day OFS at ₹382/share floor price (Aug 4–5, 2026), raising ₹31,552 crore—India's largest-ever public offering by value. The transaction increased LIC's public shareholding from 3.5% to 10%, meeting SEBI's minimum public shareholding requirement ahead of schedule and contributing substantially to FY27 disinvestment targets.
implication: Government OFS structure for large PSUs achieves MPS compliance via full green-shoe exercise (6.5% = 2.5% base + 4% oversubscription option) rather than staged tranches; floor pricing strategy (₹382 at 10% discount) absorbs institutional appetite despite initial retail hesitation; allotment mechanics (₹373.10 cut-off price) balance demand with market stability—a model for future multi-tranche PSU disinvestments.
detail: <cite index="11-4,11-5,11-6,11-7">The Indian government successfully raised Rs 31,552 crore through the LIC Offer for Sale, which closed with overwhelming investor response. The issue was oversubscribed on both days, leading to the exercise of the full green shoe option. With this, LIC's public shareholding has increased to 10 percent, achieving the minimum public shareholding requirement ahead of schedule. This marks India's largest public offering ever in terms of amount raised, with 82,23,33,558 shares allocated.</cite> <cite index="1-1,1-3">The government sold up to a 6.5% stake in Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) at a floor price of ₹382/share through a two-day offer for sale (OFS) beginning on Tuesday (August 4, 2026), with the issue opening for non-retail investors on Tuesday (August 4) and for retail investors on Wednesday (August 5).</cite> <cite index="50-1">The LIC OFS allocation price of Rs 373.10 was set as the government exercised the 4 percent oversubscription option on 5 August 2026, bringing the total LIC OFS offer to 82.21 crore shares.</cite>

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulations; specifically minimum public shareholding norms under Securities Contract (Regulations) Rules 1957, Rule 19A

structure.consideration: ₹31,552 crore (~US$3.3 billion) at allocation price of ₹373.10 per share for 82,23,33,558 shares (6.5% stake)
conditions: Base offer of 2.5% (31,62,49,885 shares) at floor price ₹382/share
Green-shoe oversubscription option of 4.0% (50,59,99,816 shares) exercisable if demand exceeds base offer
Two-day bidding: Aug 4, 2026 for non-retail investors (QIBs, mutual funds, insurance cos., corporates); Aug 5, 2026 for retail investors and eligible LIC employees
Retail investors received ₹10/share discount on cut-off price (final cut-off ₹373.10)
Oversubscription on both days permitted government to fully exercise 4% green-shoe option, raising total offer to 6.5%
Settlement on T+1 basis (Aug 6, 2026 allotment; shares credited to Demat accounts)
approvals: Union Cabinet approval (prior) for LIC OFS modality
SEBI clearance (implicit) via LIC's MPS roadmap and OFS Guidelines compliance
NSE/BSE approval for OFS listing and designated window activation
Government of India (Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services) authorization for stake sale as 'President of India, acting through Ministry of Finance'
structure.novel: First post-IPO OFS by LIC (May 2022 IPO was 3.5% dilution); full green-shoe exercise on first OFS tranche achieved within 48 hours, indicating institutional depth and sustained demand despite post-listing valuation compression; allocation price (₹373.10) at 2.37% discount to floor (₹382) despite oversubscription signals price discovery efficiency in OFS framework.

triggers.law: SEBI minimum public shareholding norms (Rule 19A, SCRR 1957)
triggers.note: Triggered May 16, 2027 deadline for 10% MPS (originally May 2024; extended by 3 years via May 2024 SEBI order); OFS achieves milestone ahead of schedule by Aug 2026
Triggered FY27 target of ₹80,000 crore; LIC OFS contributes ₹31,552 cr (~39% of annual target) and achieves two-thirds of budget estimate for miscellaneous receipts

triggers.law: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Offer for Sale Guidelines)
triggers.note: Triggered OFS structure (vs. IPO or auction) due to post-listing liquidity needs and retail participation objectives
Triggered stock exchange announcement, regulatory filings, and market transparency during 48-hour OFS window
